name: Bittersweet
lede: Bittersweet is a hot coral-orange red, named for the plant whose berries ripen red and whose English name means a taste that is both sharp and sweet.

sections.title: Name and plant
sections.body:
The books we have read say very little about this color as a color [1][2]. The one botanical link is bittersweet nightshade, *Solanum dulcamara*, whose leaves appear in a plate illustrating sap green in Baty's study of natural color charts [1]. Finlay uses the word only for taste, describing a sand palm heart as succulent and bittersweet [2].

So the books support a plant and a flavor but not a dye, a pigment or a date for the color name [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The name is first recorded in our sources in 1912, in Ridgway's standards, and later in Maerz and Paul and in ISCC-NBS [3]. The swatch #FE6F5E is a bright, warm coral [3]. It is rare in our archive of 23,781 paintings, with only 7 matches, as photographed, rarer than 72% of named colors [3]. In printed English the adjective peaks in the 2010s [3].
